items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                  In everyday life, we display behaviors with varying degrees of
goal-directedness—ranging from low-goal-directed, automated
                  <jats:italic toggle="yes">habits</jats:italic>
                  in familiar and simple tasks to highly goal-directed
                  <jats:italic toggle="yes">actions</jats:italic>
                  in novel contexts. In this study, we employed a
free-operant schedule of reinforcement combined with a reinforcer
devaluation paradigm to elicit both
                  <jats:italic toggle="yes">habits</jats:italic>
                  and
                  <jats:italic toggle="yes">actions</jats:italic>
                  ,
enabling investigation of their cognitive–neural underpinnings.
Previous research has identified two co-occurring microstructural
response types within these behaviors: bout-initiation responses and
subsequent within-bout responses. We found that readiness potential (RP)
variability decreased more markedly prior to
                  <jats:italic toggle="yes">action</jats:italic>
                  <jats:italic toggle="yes">responses</jats:italic>
                  , which contained a higher proportion of within-bout
responses, compared to
                  <jats:italic toggle="yes">habitual responses</jats:italic>
                  , which contained a
lower proportion of within-bout responses—indicating stronger neural
suppression before goal-directed
                  <jats:italic toggle="yes">actions</jats:italic>
                  than before
                  <jats:italic toggle="yes">habitual responses</jats:italic>
                  . Moreover, pre–within-bout RP variability
decreased more significantly than pre–bout-initiation RP variability,
consistent with the higher level of goal-directedness in within-bout
responses. Importantly, no significant differences were observed in
pre–within-bout RP variability between the two behavior types,
suggesting that the goal-directed nature of within-bout responses
remained stable across contexts. This underscores that the proportion of
within-bout responses is a key determinant of goal-directedness across
behavioral contexts.
                </jats:p>
title: Microstructural Response Patterns Predict Goal-Directedness
